items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: And from a very musical family too, with Tori who went on with Tony Bennett and all that.

ctx.x: I really don’t. And I bet you Donny Andre can tell you about that. And Dick Sherman will give you the history of jazz up to that point. But this was fall of ’55. And the band that came together was Em Brown, who was a senior, he was the clarinetist and the leader, Donny Andre was a sophomore and the banjo player and became the manager of the band and really did a yeoman job getting the gigs and doing all the hard work of running a band, and myself, a brand new trombonist just trying to learn how to play the…
And from a very musical family too, with Tori who went on with Tony Bennett and all that.

So then the other guy who mostly played with us was Jimmy Wormworth, and he’s sort of the guy who I think of as our drummer because Jimmy and I became very close friends. But Jimmy was my age so he was 18 starting out and he was a bop drummer. Ronnie was always a big band drummer. I mean he could play anything but he was a big band, swing band drummer. But Jimmy was a bop drummer, a wonderful drummer. And he and I became very close friends and stay in touch to this day. And he of course was the drummer for…
